flags: Stagwell acquired Freestar (Publisher First, Inc.) for $50.0 million, of which $30.0 million was paid in 3,442,043 shares of Class A Common Stock and $20.0 million in cash, with up to $60.0 million more in contingent consideration.
Stagwell raised its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance to $490 million to $540 million and its Adjusted EPS guidance to $1.07 to $1.21.
Stagwell announced the largest multi-agency deal in its history, with ServiceNow, along with a first major federal government win and an expanded Palantir partnership.

business_model.claim: Stagwell sells marketing services and technology to marketers in five areas: Marketing Services, Digital Transformation, Media & Commerce, Communications (including Advocacy), and SaaS/DaaS tools in The Marketing Cloud.
quotes: Stagwell offers the capabilities marketers need in the digital age: Marketing Services, Digital Transformation, Media & Commerce, Communications (which includes Advocacy services), and “software as a service” (“SaaS”) and “data as a service” (“DaaS”) technology tools within The Marketing Cloud.

business_model.claim: The customer base is more than 4,500 clients served by specialists in over 34 countries, and most of it is large multinational companies.
quotes: Led by entrepreneurs, our specialists in over 34 countries have a unified purpose: to drive effectiveness and improve business results for our more than 4,500 clients as of December 31, 2025.

To date, these solutions appear more geared towards addressing the needs of small and medium size businesses, rather than the large, multi-national companies that form the majority of Stagwell’s customer base.

business_model.claim: Agency work is billed as fees, and the company competes for large contracts, including multi-region contracts with annual fees above $10 million.
quotes: Our increasing global scale allows us to compete for many of the largest marketing contracts available, including multi-region contracts with annual fees in excess of $10 million.

Certain of our Brands often enter into contractual commitments with media providers and production companies and incur expenses on behalf of our clients for productions and in order to secure a variety of media time and space, in exchange for which they receive a fee.

business_model.claim: The Marketing Cloud segment sells SaaS and DaaS technology directly to in-house marketers, alongside the service businesses.
quotes: The Marketing Cloud segment delivers a comprehensive suite of technology solutions for in-house marketers, combining SaaS and DaaS offerings.

business_model.claim: The company operates through owned agency Brands, almost all of them wholly owned and the rest majority owned, with Brand management holding the remaining equity.
quotes: Stagwell holds a 100% ownership position in substantially all of its Brands, and the remainder are majority owned with management of the Brands owning the remaining equity.

business_model.claim: The company reports five operating and reportable segments: Marketing Services, Digital Transformation, Media & Commerce, Communications and The Marketing Cloud.
quotes: The Company brings itself to market and organizes its Brands into five reportable segments: “Marketing Services,” “Digital Transformation,” “Media & Commerce,” “Communications,” and “The Marketing Cloud.”

business_model.claim: In 2025, segment revenue (table in thousands) was Marketing Services $1,134,821, Media & Commerce 690,675, Communications 592,577, Digital Transformation 393,499 and The Marketing Cloud 106,537, for total revenue of $2,909,000.

quotes: “Net revenue” refers to revenue excluding billable costs.

business_model.claim: In the third quarter of 2026, revenue was $816 million and net revenue was $664 million.

business_model.claim: Revenue is concentrated in the United States. In 2025, US net revenue was $1,874,216 of $2,427,671 (table in thousands), and operations outside the United States were about 23% of revenue.
quotes: Operations outside the United States represent a significant portion of our revenues and represented approximately 23% of our revenues in 2025.

business_model.claim: Revenue is moderately concentrated: the top ten clients were about 18% of 2025 revenue, and no single customer exceeded 4%.
quotes: In the aggregate, our top ten clients based on revenue accounted for approximately 18% of our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025.
No customer represented more than 4% of total revenue.

business_model.claim: Demand depends on client marketing budgets, which move with macroeconomic conditions.
quotes: Advertising, marketing and communications expenditures are sensitive to global, national and regional macroeconomic conditions, including inflationary pressures, currency fluctuations, geopolitical uncertainty and elevated interest rates, as well as specific budgeting levels and buying patterns.

business_model.claim: Revenue moves with client wins and losses. Management names two main factors: clients' desire to change firms, and the Brands' digital and data products. The company reported net new business of $168 million in the third quarter of 2026.
quotes: We believe the two most significant factors are (i) our clients’ desire to change marketing communication firms, and (ii) the digital and data-driven products that our portfolio of marketing services firms, which we refer to as “Brands,” offer.
Net New Business of $168 million in Q3; LTM Net New Business of $586 million

business_model.claim: Revenue is seasonal. The fourth quarter is typically the highest, and political advertising lifts revenue in election cycles, most in even years.
quotes: Historically, we typically generate the highest quarterly revenue during the fourth quarter of each year.

Political advertising and related activity have also historically caused our revenue to increase during election cycles, which is most pronounced in even years, in particular during the third and fourth quarters of such years, and to decrease during other periods.

business_model.claim: The political cycle mainly hits Communications. In 2025, that segment's organic net revenue fell (16.5)%, which management attributed mainly to lower Advocacy revenue after the presidential election cycle.
quotes: These increases were partially offset by a decrease in the Communications segment, primarily reflecting lower Advocacy revenue due to political seasonality following the 2024 presidential election cycle, as well as more measured client spending and timing of project activity.

quotes: Additionally, we may be unable to hire and retain people with the skills necessary to meet the increasing client demand, and we have in the past experienced and may continue to experience wage inflation and other increases to compensation expense, which puts upward pressure on our costs and may adversely affect our profitability if we are unable to recover these increased costs.

quotes: Excluding the addition of expenses of acquired entities of $12.0 million, Office and general expenses increased $10.2 million, primarily attributable to higher software license fees due to investments in automation and AI intended to improve workflow efficiency and support future margin expansion and higher staff costs to support the growth in the business.

Media and production buying on clients' behalf creates large working-capital balances. At September 30, 2026, accounts receivable were 772,787, accrued media 228,612 and advance billings 365,529 (table in thousands).
quotes: The difference between the gross production costs and media purchases and the revenue earned by us can be significant, and primarily affects our levels of accounts receivable, expenditures billable to clients, accounts payable and accrued liabilities.

We are generally paid in arrears for our services, and if we are unable to meet our contractual requirements, we may experience delays in collection of and/or be unable to collect our client balances.

business_model.claim: Debt adds a financing cost below operating income: net interest expense was (69,587) in the nine months to September 30, 2026, with long-term debt of 1,414,574 at that date (table in thousands).

competitive_position.claim: Stagwell describes itself as a global challenger network that is transforming marketing through AI.
quotes: Stagwell Inc. is the global challenger network transforming marketing through artificial intelligence (“AI”).

competitive_position.claim: At the end of 2025 the company reported specialists in over 34 countries serving more than 4,500 clients.
quotes: Led by entrepreneurs, our specialists in over 34 countries have a unified purpose: to drive effectiveness and improve business results for our more than 4,500 clients as of December 31, 2025.

competitive_position.basis: stated in the cited item as management belief
competitive_position.claim: Management claims an advantage over legacy holding companies because it can work across business lines and geographies. It calls the traditional holding company model outdated.
quotes: We believe our ability to work across business lines and geographies gives us a competitive advantage relative to many of the legacy holding company competitors.
While legacy models still accounted for a significant share of the market in 2025, we see the traditional holding company model as outdated in this rapidly evolving industry landscape.

competitive_position.claim: The company says its global scale lets it compete for the largest marketing contracts, including multi-region contracts with annual fees above $10 million.
quotes: Our increasing global scale allows us to compete for many of the largest marketing contracts available, including multi-region contracts with annual fees in excess of $10 million.

competitive_position.claim: The company admits it is smaller than many of its larger competitors, in an industry where broad geographic and service coverage is an important competitive factor.
quotes: We are smaller than many of our larger industry competitors, and an agency’s ability to serve clients, particularly large international clients, on a broad geographic basis and across a range of services and technologies is an important competitive consideration.

competitive_position.claim: The named competitors are large global holding companies (Omnicom, WPP, Publicis, Dentsu, Havas), independent agencies, consultancies such as Accenture and Deloitte, tech platforms and media companies.
quotes: Stagwell’s Brands compete for business and talent with the operating subsidiaries of large global holding companies such as Omnicom Group Inc., WPP plc, Publicis Groupe SA, Dentsu Inc. and Havas SA, as well as with numerous independent agencies that operate in multiple markets.
Our Brands also face competition from consultancies, such as Accenture and Deloitte, tech platforms, media companies and other services firms that offer related services.

competitive_position.claim: Large IT-implementation consulting firms have entered marketing services and together hold significant market share. Management believes their lack of creative and media expertise limits them.
quotes: In recent years, a number of large consulting firms with information technology implementation backgrounds have entered the marketing services market and, collectively, achieved significant market share.

competitive_position.claim: Major technology companies such as Amazon and Meta offer alternative marketing solutions. The company says these so far target small and medium businesses rather than its large multinational client base.
quotes: Additionally, major technology companies, such as Amazon and Meta, have entered the market, offering alternative marketing solutions to clients.

To date, these solutions appear more geared towards addressing the needs of small and medium size businesses, rather than the large, multi-national companies that form the majority of Stagwell’s customer base.

competitive_position.claim: Barriers to entry are described as minimal because an agency's main asset is its people. Small brands can sometimes take business from larger competitors.
quotes: We also compete with smaller businesses that operate in local or regional markets, and because an agency’s principal asset is often its people, barriers to entry are minimal, and relatively small brands are, on occasion, able to take all or some portion of a client’s business from a larger competitor.

competitive_position.claim: Competitors may discount their services, which could force the company to accept lower margins or lose clients.
quotes: Price competition could force us to choose between lowering our prices (and suffering reduced operating margins) or losing a client’s business.

competitive_position.claim: Clients put their business up for competitive review from time to time, and the company has lost accounts in such reviews.
quotes: Many companies, including companies with which we have long-standing relationships, put their advertising and marketing communications business up for competitive review from time to time, and we have lost client accounts in the past as a result of such reviews.

competitive_position.claim: The top ten clients were about 18% of 2025 revenue, and no single customer exceeded 4%.

No customer represented more than 4% of total revenue.
